Equinix raised both '26 and long-term rev and AFFO growth guidance on strong momentum and broad enterprise demand for capacity. Increased capex to $5-7bn annually over '27 - '29 as demand signals remain robust. Raise rev ests modestly, PT remains $1,250, reiterate OW with 3x risk/reward skew.
Key Takeaways
EQIX delivered $424mn in annualized gross bookings (+23% y/y) vs $369mn MSe. +9.7k net interconnections and 11% y/y monthly recurring rev vs. 11.6% y/y MSe.
- '26 rev growth guide +50bps to 10.7%-11.6% y/y. LT guide raised 10-13% annual rev growth, '29 53%+ Adj. EBITDA margin, $5bn-$7bn annual capex, 9-12% AFFO/sh.
EQIX outlined broad enterprise AI adoption as tenants run open models on private AI infrastructure, deploy sovereign AI stacks, train models and reduce latency.
8 of the top 10 AI model providers and neoclouds are running workloads within Equinix facilities. We see scaled interconnection network as a key driver.
■ Reiterate OW with a mid-'27 $1,250 PT, an implied ~25x fwd. AFFO and ~26x fwd. EBITDA. Bull case to $1,500 implies ~50% upside and ~28x fwd. AFFO.

Impact on investment outlook: EQIX remains our Top Pick within our Communications Infrastructure coverage. We continue to see inflecting AI inference workloads proliferating across enterprises and serving as a rising tide of capacity demand for scaled and powered colocation data center operators. 2Q results, with 23% y/y growth in gross bookings and a record addition of 9,700 net

interconnection, further strengthen this view. 8 of the top 10 AI model providers and 8 of the top 10 neoclouds are running key networking workloads in Equinix facilities. We continue to see proliferating AI use cases, and in particular latency-sensitive demand, to serve as a tailwind to revenue and AFFO growth. We reiterate OW, see an attractive 3x risk/reward skew and maintain our mid'27 price of $1,250, an implied ~25x fwd. AFFO or ~26x fwd. EBITDA.

was in line with estimates and total '26 revenue growth guidance raised by 50bps to 10.7% - 11.6% y/y and increased its AFFO/share growth outlook to 11.4% - 12.9%. Longer term, Equinix raised its '27 - '29 targets from the prior analyst day last June and now expects 10% - 13% annual revenue growth, a 53%+ adjusted EBITDA margin by '29, $5bn - $7bn of annual capex, and 9% - 12% annual AFFO/share growth.
Equinix highlighted four distinct enterprise AI use cases emerging across its customer base:
- Stack: Enterprises are running open models on private AI infrastructure to reduce token costs.
- Sovereign: Enterprises are deploying sovereign AI stacks to satisfy data residency and compliance requirements.
- Batch: Customers are deploying AI "centers of excellence" and AI factories for model training and batch inferencing at Equinix.
- Latency sensitive: Enterprises are placing inference infrastructure within specific metros to reduce latency and lower data backhaul costs.

Capex was again increased to accelerate capacity delivery: Equinix incurred $1.6bn of capex in 2Q, bringing 1H26 spending to approximately $2.8bn, and raised its 2026 total capex guidance to $5.0bn - $6.0bn from our prior estimate of $4.1bn. Roughly 90% of quarterly capex was directed toward expansion, with Equinix planning to double cabinet deliveries in 2H and accelerate more than 7,000 cabinets previously scheduled for 2027 into 4Q26 (see Exhibit 2 for our expansion tracker). Equinix plans to increase leverage by approximately a turn by '29, and we model an increase in net debt of ~$13bn and net debt / EBITDA by YE29 at ~4.7x.

Notably, it continues to expect ~25% cash-on-cash returns within three to four years of assets entering service, while the stabilized portfolio currently generates a 27% yield. Sustaining mid-20's stabilized yields is key to further positive estimate revisions ahead (as previously discussed in our capex yield analysis here). See Exhibit 1 for upside to revenue estimates if Equinix is, in fact, able to bring capacity online at this rate at a stabilized yield of ~25%.

Given the accelerated cabinet delivery schedule, we have raised our '26 revenue growth estimate 50bps to 11.6% y/y from 11.1% y/y. The capex guide implies Equinix utilizes 1 GW of its 3 GW controlled land portfolio by '29, including ~700 MW currently under construction and ~300 MW by the expanded capex plan. In our base case, we now expect a 12.5% revenue CAGR from '26 - '29, and in our bull case assume a 14% CAGR, driving approximately $63 of AFFO/share by '29. As total debt needed to fund expansion increases, AFFO/share estimates are largely unchanged from prior estimates.
See Exhibit 4 for 2Q26 results vs. expectations and Exhibit 6 for changes to our estimates.
